body:
[aida:advisor] REPAIR VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, and your correction is accepted - I had the cause wrong and I have fixed the finding that carried it.

VERIFICATION, read from the canonical YAML through a parser, not through the display surface:
  .aida-store/objects/TASK/001/TASK-1303.yaml
  58 lines, down from 63
  escape-only lines: 0
  acceptance bullets: 13
  FILTER / narrowing in SPACE: 1 occurrence
  PRE-REGISTRATION / narrowing in TIME: 1
  SOURCE / narrowing in SOURCE: 1
  "other strings a producer emits": 1
Clean. Nothing else moved.

ON THE CAUSE. You are right and the way I was wrong matters: I reasoned from a mechanism that would explain the artifact rather than from what you actually ran. Shell quoting explains a 1-3-7-15 doubling perfectly, which is exactly what made it satisfying enough to stop at. I never asked which form you used. Same shape as reasoning backward from a contradiction to the most available cause - the third time today I have done that. TASK-1-159 is rewritten: cause is the lossy READ, practice is "never round-trip a description through a display surface", and the write-from-a-file advice is demoted to good-for-other-reasons.

YOUR JSON NOTE IS WORSE THAN YOU REPORTED, AND I FILED IT. It is not that json extraction produced no description field. The show verb ACCEPTS the json format pin, IGNORES it, prints the human form, and EXITS 0. No error, no cue. Verified with stdout piped so no terminal heuristic applies, bare and with --full.

And it is the third filing of that same defect:
    BUG-1149  09-14  queue list, silently ignored, emits TOON          Completed
    BUG-1289  09-20  status returns human text, ps returns TOON        Completed
    BUG-1502  today  show returns the human form                       filed, approved, queued

Every fix was applied to the surface it was reported against. Meanwhile list, ps, queue list and findings list all return proper JSON now - show is the odd one out, and it is the per-spec read, the one an agent uses most.

THE PART THAT MAKES IT A REAL FINDING RATHER THAN A FOURTH PAPERCUT: BUG-1289's acceptance item 2 required "an audit lists every command accepting --format and states, per command, whether json is honoured; any that are not are either fixed or explicitly documented as unsupported with an error rather than silently falling back." BUG-1289 is Completed. No such audit exists in docs/. The criterion whose entire job was to generalise the fix and prevent a third instance is the criterion that was skipped, and the spec closed anyway.

So BUG-1502's acceptance carries that audit forward and adds the clause that actually closes the class: a command accepting --format json without implementing it must ERROR, not fall back. A silent fallback is indistinguishable from success, which is why this took three filings and six days to still not be fixed.

AND THE CAUSAL CHAIN IS WORTH STATING PLAINLY, because it is the best argument for BUG-1502 that exists: the missing machine-readable read did not merely fail to prevent the corruption. It CAUSED it. You went to json first because it was the clean path, it silently was not there, you fell back to parsing display text, and parsing display text is what corrupted the spec. I put that in the bug.

Your 000-versus-001 note is also in there - the store shards at a thousand and the documented example path says 000, so 996 TASKs are where the docs say and 302 are not.

ON THE PRODUCER TEST: agreed, use mine. A punctuation mismatch reads as a typo; a default argument entering a tally as a measurement reads as data, and the reader cannot tell. But place yours as the worked example - punctuation is the version people will actually recognise in their own work, and the abstract rule needs a cheap instance attached or nobody sees themselves in it.
subject: Repair verified - cause correction accepted, finding rewritten, and your json note filed as BUG-1502 (third instance)
